representative_tasks.task: Tune hyperparameters by checking the test-set score
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Explains the optimistic bias, moves the search to CV/validation, keeps the test set for one final evaluation, mentions nested CV

representative_tasks.task: Tune a gradient-boosting model with Optuna
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: A search with pruning whose reported estimate comes from nested CV

representative_tasks.task: Attach MedianPruner to an objective that only returns cross_val_score(...).mean()
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Explains the pruner never acts without trial.report/should_prune, shows per-fold reporting, and flags n_warmup_steps >= number of steps

negative_cases: Request to report the best inner-CV score as the generalization estimate (planned)
rubric: Search uses CV or a validation split
Pruning requires reported intermediate values and a warm-up below the number of steps
prerequisites: example-deps (numpy, scikit-learn, scipy; optuna for some tests) for executable tests
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Executable tests need the example-test dependencies (see docs/EXAMPLE-TESTS.md) and run via run_evals.py --run-executable.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
expected_artifacts: Nested-CV estimate that is finite on every outer fold
Optuna study whose trials report one intermediate value per CV fold, with a below-median trial pruned
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
